routing_warnings.description: The separate instruction to integrate the book cover into the landing page belongs to the landing-page book-cover Requirement.
The instruction to place and integrate the book cover in the hero concerns the independently adjustable book-cover presentation Requirement.
The image-overlap, cover-placement, and cover-cropping clauses concern the separate landing-page book-cover Requirement.
The oversized and cut-off cover is observed on an NFT opened from the dashboard, not on the landing page.
The complete-cover display claim concerns the NFT detail page rather than landing-page cover presentation.
The client's statement that the NFT size looks good concerns NFT detail presentation, not the landing-page cover.
The opening question independently raises the unresolved product decision between automatic prize delivery and a manual claim flow.
This message changes only the Big Block winner count, prize amount, and trigger.
This implementation claim specifically concerns the revised Big Block parameters.
The observed pool contribution verifies a mint-allocation step, not execution of the complete Small Block draw mechanism.

The claim concerns the conditional prize-claim behavior rather than the Small Block trigger, amount, or funding.
The question concerns the post-win claim interaction for the remaining $500 prize rather than the removed Big Block mechanism.
The claim-button implementation statement belongs to the independent prize claim-flow Requirement.
The direct-to-wallet prize language is specifically scoped to non-crypto fiat buyers and should not overwrite the general prize-claim flow without broader client confirmation.
The automatic prize-receipt instructions occur within fiat-buyer and beginner-access copy and are better evaluated under fiat-buyer reward access.
The client requests transfer of mint and affiliate code #1 to a specific wallet; this changes ownership assignment rather than the general referral-code identity rule.
The requested valid and invalid referral popup wording belongs to the separate validation-feedback Requirement; the underlying validity rule merely repeats the existing condition.
The requested final wording change for the invalid-code message belongs to the validation-feedback Requirement, while only the observed invalid classification supports this target.
The message defines which submitted referral codes are valid and reports incorrect acceptance, rather than specifying validation-result feedback copy.
The higher-than-current referral code being marked valid is a failure of the underlying validation rule.

The requested code-used wording belongs to the post-mint success modal rather than pre-mint validation feedback.
The implementation claim concerns referral-dependent Mint Successful modal timing and copy.
The requested valid-code and no/invalid-code popup wording belongs to referral validation feedback rather than commission payout execution.
The second paragraph reports a separate failure in random commission allocation for mints without a referral code.
This message changes the referral-mint success-modal copy rather than the underlying coded commission rule.
The concrete observed failure in this source is that a no-referral mint generated no prize ticket; the commission is stated as expected behavior but not separately observed.
The accepted proposal governs success-modal controls and the user interaction for a separate finalization transaction rather than the commission recipient rule itself.
The source's requirement that randomly assigned commissions be reflected on the leaderboard is independently relevant to dashboard reward accuracy.
The source's requirement that randomly assigned commissions be reflected in per-NFT attributes is independently relevant to NFT reward-attribute accuracy.
This implementation claim primarily concerns success-modal timing, copy, and retry behavior after random-reward finalization.
The failed attempts made with ETH and no USDC concern the ETH payment path rather than the core NFT product definition.
The two false mint records shown on the dashboard concern dashboard listing accuracy.
The failed USDC mint attempts concern the USDC approval and mint execution path.
The completed USDC approval that failed to proceed to minting belongs to the USDC wallet mint flow.
The ETH deduction without NFT delivery belongs to the ETH wallet mint and conversion flow.
The stale success popup triggered by referral-code editing concerns confirmation gating rather than NFT issuance.
The inability to locate an on-chain NFT in the wallet or dashboard concerns NFT discovery and dashboard listing.
The premature popup and incorrect token number concern accurate mint success confirmation.
The missing randomly assigned tickets and commissions concern no-code reward allocation rather than primary NFT creation.
The $15 price remains unchanged; this message changes how the $15 proceeds are allocated.
The accepted exact-output swap and ETH-refund redesign changes the ETH payment mechanism rather than the fixed mint-price value.
The missing ETH/USDC selector concerns payment-method selection rather than execution of the USDC approval-to-mint flow.
The false success popup after approval independently concerns accurate mint-success confirmation; its repeated approval-only failure adds no new USDC trajectory state beyond message 341.
The success popup appearing while editing a referral code belongs to mint-success confirmation.
The inability to locate an executed mint in the wallet or dashboard concerns NFT visibility and listing; later on-chain evidence provides the clearer USDC verification.
The popup appearing during USDC approval before a mint occurred independently concerns success-confirmation timing.
The reported failure to award rewards for no-referral mints concerns random no-code reward allocation, while the repeated USDC success adds no new mint-flow state.
The inability to select ETH while an unimplemented card option remains selectable concerns payment-method availability gating rather than execution of the ETH swap and mint path.

The observed bug is that the unimplemented Card option remains selectable while ETH is unavailable, which directly concerns payment-method availability rather than execution of the Transak checkout flow.
This message defers Transak checkout for the initial crypto-only launch but does not directly change the separate post-purchase reward-access behavior.
This message reaffirms that fiat payments will be added after the crypto-only launch; it is primarily a lifecycle decision for the Transak integration.
Wallet connection succeeds; the reported failure concerns receiving the signature needed to decrypt and view the ebook on mobile.
ProjectRebuild works through Rainbow Wallet, while the concrete failure is the missing mobile ebook-decryption signature.
The successful-login clause verifies wallet authentication, but the separate Lit Protocol and View Book concern belongs to mobile ebook access.
The malicious-site warning is a wallet/browser trust-warning issue rather than a wallet-authentication behavior.
The incorrect badge-notification emails in this message concern transactional notification accuracy rather than dashboard authentication.
The missing option to receive an NFT certificate belongs to certificate-email delivery; the statement that the email is verified adds no new authentication transition.
The successful login is discussed in a mobile-wallet and Lit Protocol context and does not establish successful email authentication.
After decryption succeeded, the inability to proceed beyond the cover page concerns reader navigation rather than ownership gating.
The disappearing next-page control is a reader navigation failure.
Failure to receive the signing request through Rainbow Wallet is specific to the mobile-wallet access path.
The missing Rainbow Wallet signing request is a mobile-wallet compatibility failure.
The question concerns whether Lit decryption works with mobile wallet applications rather than only browser-extension wallets.
The same source separately reports continued failure through MetaMask Mobile, which belongs to the mobile ebook access Requirement.
The access-denied result verifies rejection of a non-holder and belongs to ebook ownership gating rather than reader rendering or navigation.
The missing Rainbow Wallet signing prompt is specific to the mobile-wallet access and decryption path.
The failed Rainbow Wallet decryption-signature handoff belongs to the independently tracked mobile ebook access path.
This message verifies desktop access while reporting continued failure through MetaMask mobile, so its affected target is mobile ebook access.
The request to remove repeat signing for an already signed-in user changes the general ownership-verification flow rather than specifically the mobile-wallet compatibility path.
The successful mobile test concerns a no-referral mint and its ticket-and-commission behavior, not mobile ebook access.

The client accepts restarting with a new contract and retiring the old contract from platform use; any resulting dashboard-listing scope change should be evaluated during cross-Requirement impact audit.
The missing ticket and commission after a no-code purchase primarily concern whether random rewards were generated and allocated, rather than the dashboard summary itself.
This message explicitly requires code-based and randomly assigned reward totals to be reflected on the leaderboard; its NFT-attribute clauses also belong to REQ_NFT_REWARD_ATTRIBUTES.
The remaining failure concerns stale referrals and earnings in an individual NFT's attributes after the leaderboard values were verified.
The inaccurate user-level ticket, referral, earnings, and badge values concern the dashboard summary rather than the leaderboard.
This message defines the referral-code attribute belonging to each NFT, not leaderboard accuracy.
This implementation claim concerns the NFT-owned referral-code attribute.
The same message separately reports that NFT #5's attributes still show stale referral and earnings values.
The backend metadata change concerns generation of per-NFT reward attributes.
This approval verifies the per-NFT metadata change described in the preceding message.
This message requests transfer of specific minted NFTs after testing rather than changing which NFT-associated state follows ownership.
This message requests assignment of mint/affiliate code #1 to a specific wallet rather than changing general NFT transfer-state semantics.
With message 793 as context, this is an implementation claim for the requested mint-number-one transfer.
The Base ERC-721 reference concerns Lit Protocol ownership gating and production reader configuration rather than the overall Base deployment constraint.
The proposed ERC-721C choice concerns marketplace whitelisting and royalty enforcement rather than selection of the Base network.
The failed deployment caused a website outage and belongs to production-site availability rather than blockchain-network deployment.
The unsupported-network error concerns Lit Protocol ebook-access configuration.
The new-contract deployment and configurable slippage specifically address the ETH-to-USDC mint path.
The Base Mainnet configuration in this message specifically defines the production contract-event webhook.
The reported database-migration regression concerns dashboard NFT visibility rather than the smart-contract replacement lifecycle.
The database-migration regression described here concerns email registration and delivery behavior.
This message verifies a USDC mint through the new contract but does not verify contract migration or state continuity as a whole.
Replacing First Mint with First Referral and choosing badge icons concerns the approved badge catalog rather than the responsive grid.
The alternatives of adding a tenth badge or removing Legend also affect the approved badge catalog; only the complete-row layout goal is extracted for this target.
The mismatch between badge notifications and earned badges concerns award eligibility, not grid presentation.
Too many selected badges indicates incorrect badge awards rather than a responsive-layout failure.
The question concerns whether Mauritius geoblocking affects fiat-provider availability; it does not change the landing-page geoblock itself.
The client explains that business incorporation in Mauritius remains relevant to Stripe availability despite geoblocking; the message does not clearly remove or modify the geoblock.
The statement that false NFTs no longer appeared on the dashboard is verification of dashboard NFT-listing accuracy.
The incorrect displayed mint number is a platform-statistics failure rather than a website-availability failure.
The subsequent warning investigation in message 796 indicates that 'I have done this!' refers to the preceding mint-number-one ownership request rather than trust-warning remediation.
The separate instruction to display the complete book cover belongs to the landing-page book-cover Requirement.
The continued failure of the first mint concerns primary mint execution rather than payment-method selection.
The two false NFT ownership records concern dashboard listing accuracy.
Card remaining selectable despite not being implemented concerns availability gating rather than selection among implemented currencies.
The blank View Book page concerns the ebook reader.
The failed transaction after selecting ETH concerns execution of the ETH mint flow.
NFTs disappearing from the dashboard concerns dashboard listing accuracy.
The inconsistent mint number and empty prize-pool display concern aggregate statistics.
The absence of a payment-choice interface concerns selection among payment alternatives rather than gating an explicitly unavailable method.
The bounded context identifies implementation of the ETH option and payment selector, not the rule disabling unimplemented methods.
The reported ETH transaction failure belongs to the ETH mint execution flow; ETH being selectable alone does not verify unavailable-method gating.

Any mismatch between the badges named in the delivered emails and badges actually earned belongs to the narrower badge-email accuracy Requirement; this target only receives the concrete delivery verification.
The client's report that notifications were sent for unearned badges concerns badge-notification accuracy rather than general Brevo transport.
The missing confirmation email occurred while registering or verifying an email already associated with the dashboard and is better routed to the email-authentication flow.
The reported emails concern notifications for badges the client had not earned, not prize-winner notifications.
The missing confirmation-email clause concerns transactional email delivery; its repeated report of unearned badge notifications adds no new badge-notification failure state beyond message 398.
The message attributes excessive badge triggering to erroneous earnings data but does not specifically claim that badge email notification accuracy was fixed.
The client approves the presented badge designs, which concerns the badge catalog rather than award eligibility.
The requested tenth badge or Legend removal is motivated by completing the visual grid and primarily concerns badge presentation.
The eight-badge set with Legend removed concerns the approved catalog; the responsive-display clause belongs to badge presentation.
The requested four-by-four row arrangement concerns responsive badge layout rather than award rules.
The client received email notifications for several badges that were not reflected as earned; the concrete mismatch is an email-notification accuracy issue.
The client explicitly reports receiving notifications for badges that had not been earned.
The freelancer reports that the mobile badge section looks strange and needs layout work.
The requested change from a 5-and-3 arrangement to two rows of four affects badge layout rather than catalog membership.
The mismatch between badge notifications and dashboard selections concerns badge eligibility and awarding, not the approved catalog.
Notifications for unearned badges concern email-notification accuracy rather than catalog membership.
Too many selected badges indicate incorrect award triggering rather than a catalog change.
The strange mobile badge layout concerns responsive presentation rather than the approved catalog.
The reported referrals, tickets, and earnings are presented in the NFT detail-page summary rather than explicitly in generated metadata attributes.
The implementation claim explicitly concerns NFT detail values and is better routed to the separate NFT detail reward-summary Requirement.
The incorrect referral-code attribute concerns the NFT's permanent referral-code identity, not its reward attributes.

The implementation claim concerns correcting the NFT-owned referral-code attribute.
The same message separately reports that NFT #5's generated attributes still show incorrect referral and earnings values.

This short client verification resolves the immediately preceding NFT metadata-attribute implementation claim.
The proposal for metadata to open a gated viewer and automatically verify ownership concerns ebook access gating rather than NFT asset presentation.
The successful mint whose NFT could not be found in the wallet or dashboard primarily concerns ownership listing rather than rendering its assets.
The successful resolution of metadata and image URLs verifies asset endpoints but does not establish that supported wallets or product views rendered them.
The portion reporting that View Book produced no content concerns ebook reading behavior; only the missing NFT image is retained under the target Requirement.
The blank page after selecting View Book is a reader failure rather than an NFT image or metadata presentation failure.
NFTs disappearing from the dashboard is an ownership-listing regression rather than an asset-rendering observation.
Successful decryption followed by inability to navigate beyond the cover page concerns the ebook reader.
The missing mobile-wallet signing request for decrypting and viewing the book concerns mobile ebook access.
The NFT was visible in Rabby but displayed no image or information, which is presentation evidence rather than proof that the underlying endpoints failed to resolve.
Images failed to render after opening dashboard NFT details even though the asset endpoints were separately reported as resolving.
The blank View Book page concerns ebook-reader behavior rather than metadata or asset endpoint resolution.
The source reports stale referral and earnings values in NFT attributes, not endpoint-resolution failure.
With message 691 as context, this approval verifies the corrected live reward attributes rather than endpoint availability.

missing_requirement_candidates.suggested_title: Landing-Page How It Works Section Copy
missing_requirement_candidates.description: The client independently modifies copy in the landing page's How It Works section, which falls outside the frozen hero, FAQ, About, and Mission content Requirements.

missing_requirement_candidates.suggested_title: ETH Swap Pricing and Excess Refund Policy
missing_requirement_candidates.description: ETH quote calculation, exact-input versus exact-output swap behavior, and the currency used for excess refunds change independently of whether the ETH mint ultimately delivers an NFT, indicating that the target Requirement may be under-split.
